mimic-44767658.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at 60 bpm: a small atrial spike precedes every beat and is followed by a low-amplitude P wave. No intrinsic atrial activity is visible.
mimic-44767658.av_relationship: AV sequential: atrial spike, then ventricular spike about 180-190 ms later, on every beat.

II, III and aVF: negative, so the frontal axis is northwest (cart -146). Paced QRS about 190-200 ms (cart 236 ms). Negative I plus R in V1 plus a northwest axis means LV capture, with an apical (RV) component pulling V3-V6 and the inferior leads negative. That is the usual biventricular pattern, and the doublet ventricular artifact suggests two ventricular outputs. Against this, the very broad QRS with a slurred R in V1 would also fit LV-only (epicardial) capture with loss of RV capture. Moderate certainty: about 60% BiV, 40% LV-only.
mimic-44767658.malfunction_evidence: Every atrial and ventricular spike is followed by its chamber's depolarisation, and timing is constant (A-A 1000 ms, AV ~185 ms). No pauses.
mimic-44767658.rates: Lower rate 60 bpm (RR 1000 ms). Paced AV interval (A spike to V spike) about 180-190 ms.
teaching_points: AV sequential (DDD) pacing: every beat has an atrial spike, a P wave, a ventricular spike and a wide QRS.
Paced QRS that is negative in lead I with a dominant R in V1 and a northwest axis means the LV is being captured, which is the CRT pattern.
An RV-apical-only paced QRS would be LBBB-like (QS in V1, positive I). Its absence here points to LV involvement.
A very wide (>180-200 ms) RBBB-like paced QRS should prompt a check for loss of RV capture (LV-only pacing).
mimic-44767658.notes: Clean tracing with mild high-frequency noise. The site call (BiV vs LV-only) rests mainly on QRS width, so it is moderately uncertain.

The spike at 0.29 s is followed 100 ms later by a conducted beat, and those at 4.97 and 5.73 s by conducted beats within the AV delay. Ventricular-paced complexes after V spikes at about 3.75 and 4.51 s (spike ~305 ms after the atrial spike) are relatively narrow and likely fused with conducted beats. V1 shows only a small notched R, not the classic QS of RV pacing. QRS about 110-150 ms. The beats at 3.75 and 4.51 s are narrower than the native RBBB QRS, which suggests fusion of RV pacing with conducted beats. Not enough cleanly paced beats for a firm site call. Low certainty.

mimic-43878645.malfunction_evidence: Atrial spikes at ~0.29, 3.44, 4.21, 4.97 and 5.73 s are not followed by any P wave. Because the atrium is fibrillating, non-capture is expected (functional). Atrial pacing during AF itself shows the fibrillatory signal is not being sensed or the device has not mode-switched. Ventricular sensing and capture appear appropriate.
mimic-43878645.rates: Atrial spike interval about 760-770 ms (~78 bpm) when pacing. Programmed AV delay about 300-330 ms. AF ventricular response irregular, about 85-95 bpm.
teaching_points: Atrial pacing spikes in AF cannot capture: the atrium is already fibrillating (functional non-capture, not lead failure).
Atrial pacing during AF means the device is not sensing the fibrillatory signal (atrial undersensing) or has not mode-switched.
Long AV delays (AV search/hysteresis) let conducted beats inhibit ventricular pacing, which produces fusion beats.
mimic-43878645.notes: A complex, busy tracing: AF with RBBB conduction, one PVC, atrial spikes that do not capture, and a few paced or fused ventricular beats. Atrial undersensing is inferred from atrial pacing during AF; no device interrogation is available. The ventricular site is uncertain.

mimic-41788025.atrial_rhythm: Sinus/atrial rhythm with intermittent atrial pacing. Early beats are irregular, probably sinus or atrial ectopy with P waves hidden in the preceding T waves. Later beats are preceded by small atrial spikes at ~750-800 ms intervals.
mimic-41788025.av_relationship: Mixed. Early on, P-synchronous (atrial-sensed) ventricular pacing at irregular rates. From ~4.4 s onward mostly AV sequential pacing, with atrial spike to ventricular spike about 150 ms.

mimic-41788025.site_evidence: Lead I: small, mainly negative (QS/qr). V1: dominant R with a slurred upstroke, then an abrupt S. V2: R/S. V3: rS. V4-V6: deep QS. Negative I plus R in V1 plus a northwest axis indicates LV capture. The modest width and apical-type negativity in V4-V6 and the inferior leads favour simultaneous RV-apex plus LV pacing over LV-only, which is usually wider. Doubled V artifacts support two ventricular outputs. Moderate certainty.
mimic-41788025.malfunction_evidence: Every ventricular spike captures with the same morphology. Atrial spikes are small, and the P waves after them are not clearly seen, so atrial capture cannot be confirmed but there is no evidence of failure.
mimic-41788025.rates: Ventricular paced rate 75-120 bpm (RR 500-800 ms). AV sequential at ~750-800 ms (~75-80 bpm), AV interval ~150 ms.
teaching_points: BiV/CRT pacing: paced QRS negative in lead I, R wave in V1, northwest axis, relatively narrow paced QRS.
Compare with RV apical pacing: QS in V1, positive lead I, LBBB-like.
Dual-chamber CRT devices both track sensed P waves and pace AV sequentially at the lower rate.
mimic-41788025.notes: Atrial spikes are small, and atrial capture is hard to confirm. The early irregular rate suggests tracking of sinus beats or PACs.

mimic-40923113.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at 60 bpm. Each atrial spike is followed by a small P wave (atrial capture).
mimic-40923113.av_relationship: Atrial pacing with intrinsic AV conduction. Spike-to-QRS about 220-230 ms (long AV conduction), no ventricular spikes.
mimic-40923113.beats: All 10 beats are atrial paced: spikes at about 0.24, 1.24, 2.24 ... 9.24 s, each followed by a P wave and a narrow conducted QRS (~94 ms). No ventricular pacing, PVCs or fusion.

mimic-40923113.notes: Clean, simple example of atrial pacing with own AV conduction.

mimic-48503996.atrial_rhythm: Not visible: heavy 60-Hz interference obscures P waves. Underlying atrial rhythm undetermined.
mimic-48503996.beats: Ventricular paced beats (very large, probably unipolar spikes followed by a wide QRS) at about 1.00, 1.72, 3.00, 3.71, 5.00, 5.72, 7.14, 7.86, 8.57 and 9.29 s. A non-capturing spike at about 6.43 s falls ~150-190 ms after the onset of the 6.27-s beat.
mimic-48503996.mode: VVI demand pacing: pacing interval ~710 ms (~84 bpm), reset by sensed beats at 0.29, 2.29 and 4.29 s.
mimic-48503996.site_evidence: Paced QRS about 150 ms, LBBB-like: QS in V1-V4, rS in V5, R in V6. Lead I and aVL tall positive. II, III and aVF negative, so a left superior axis (cart -79). Classic RV apical pacing. Confident.
mimic-48503996.malfunction_evidence: The non-paced beats at 0.29, 2.29 and 4.29 s are sensed (the next spike comes ~0.71 s later). The beat at ~6.27 s is not sensed: a spike is delivered at ~6.43 s, exactly one pacing interval after the 5.72-s paced beat, inside that beat's QRS/ST, and it does not capture (ventricle refractory). This may reflect late local sensing of an ectopic beat, but on the surface ECG it behaves as undersensing.
teaching_points: Demand (VVI) pacing: intrinsic beats reset the timing, and the next spike follows one escape interval later.
Undersensing: a spike delivered at the programmed interval despite a preceding beat. If it falls in the refractory period it does not capture (functional non-capture).
RV apical paced morphology: LBBB-like with a superior axis.
Large unipolar spikes and 60-Hz noise can make tracings hard to read.
mimic-48503996.notes: Heavy 60-Hz noise and saturating spikes. Only one undersensing event. The non-paced beats (wide, QS in II/V1) may be PVCs or conducted beats with bundle-branch block; the P waves cannot be seen to decide.

mimic-42824496.av_relationship: P-synchronous (atrial-sensed) ventricular pacing. P onset to V spike about 160-170 ms.
mimic-42824496.beats: All 11 beats are atrial-sensed, ventricular-paced with identical morphology: V spikes at about 0.37, 1.30, 2.20 ... s, every ~920 ms. No intrinsic, PVC or clearly fused beats.

The narrow width suggests constant fusion with native conduction (AV delay close to PR), LV pacing from an inferior/middle cardiac vein site, or LV-septal/left posterior fascicle area capture. mimic-42824496.rates: About 65 bpm (RR ~920 ms). AV (P to V spike) about 160-170 ms.

A dominant R in V1 during ventricular pacing is not the expected RV pattern. Consider LV lead pacing, septal or conduction-system capture, fusion, or lead malposition.
A narrow paced QRS should prompt you to consider fusion with intrinsic conduction.
mimic-42824496.notes: The mode is clear. The ventricular site is genuinely uncertain (confidence ~2 for the site). This needs comparison with a native ECG or device information.

mimic-43087828.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm (sinus tachycardia borderline) at ~90 bpm. Upright P waves in V1 and II.
mimic-43087828.av_relationship: Sinus P waves conducted with PR ~170 ms. Tiny ventricular spikes fall at or just after QRS onset.

Small spikes at or just after QRS onset are visible in II/aVF on most beats (e.g. ~1.0, 1.66, 2.33, 3.0 s ...). The QRS is not changed by the spike (beats with and without a visible spike look the same), so they are pseudofusion beats. No fully paced beats.
mimic-43087828.mode: Atrial-tracking ventricular pacing (VDD/DDD) with AV delay about equal to intrinsic PR, giving pseudofusion. Alternatively demand ventricular pacing with spikes coinciding with native QRS.
mimic-43087828.site_evidence: No paced morphology to judge: QRS ~100 ms, notched, positive in I/II/aVF, QS/rS with notches in V1, tall R in V4-V6, identical with or without a visible spike.
mimic-43087828.malfunction_evidence: Pseudofusion is normal device behaviour when the AV delay is close to the intrinsic PR. It is not undersensing: the spike falls before the RV lead senses the local activation.
teaching_points: Pseudofusion: a pacing spike falls on an intrinsic QRS without changing its shape. The spike is ineffective but this is not a malfunction.
This happens when the programmed AV delay is about equal to the patient's own PR interval.
Pseudofusion is easily mistaken for undersensing. Check whether the spike falls within the first part of the QRS.
mimic-43087828.notes: The spikes are small and filtered, and best seen in II and aVF on the 50 mm/s zoom. The cart detected them ('Demand pacing').

teaching_points: In CRT, a paced QRS with a q in lead I and a positive V1 indicates LV capture.

LV-origin PVCs (RBBB-like) reach the RV lead late, so a spike can appear well inside the QRS.

mimic-44402742.beats: All about 12 beats are atrial paced (spikes at about 0.17, 1.03, 1.88, 2.73 s and so on), then conducted QRS with RBBB about 220 ms later. No ventricular-paced, PVC or clearly fused beats.
mimic-44402742.notes: The cart said 'Demand pacing' but saw only the atrial spikes.
teaching_points: Atrial pacing spike, then paced P, then native conducted QRS

mimic-44536694.av_relationship: Probably P-synchronous. Every other P conducts with PR about 190-200 ms (bifascicular-block morphology). mimic-44536694.ventricular_site: RV apex likely for the paced beats (possibly fused with native conduction)

The alternating non-paced beats have a tall R in V1, upright I and deep QS inferiorly (RBBB plus LAFB pattern).

mimic-44536694.beats: Ventricular-paced beats (with spike) at about 0.39, 1.88, 3.34, 4.08, 4.83, 6.25, 7.74 and 9.2 s. Pattern is mostly bigeminal (B A B A B B B A B A ...).
mimic-44536694.rates: Ventricular rate about 82 bpm; paced-to-paced interval about 0.73 s
mimic-44536694.notes: An alternative reading is ventricular pacing with LV-origin bigeminal PVCs (PACED_PVC), if the P waves are not real. The P waves are subtle, so the mode is uncertain.
teaching_points: Alternating paced and native beats
Bifascicular block morphology in the conducted beats

mimic-43035373.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm about 77 bpm, P waves before every QRS

Its timing (about 730 ms after the previous QRS) does not fit a ventricular escape interval, because other sinus RRs of 780-790 ms are not paced. mimic-43155662.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm/sinus tachycardia about 96 bpm, small P waves just before each ventricular spike
mimic-43155662.mode: DDD/VDD with atrial-sensed (P-synchronous) biventricular pacing and a short sensed AV delay (about 100-120 ms from P onset)
mimic-43155662.site_evidence: The paced QRS is relatively narrow, about 100-110 ms (machine 102 ms). V1 shows a dominant initial R followed by S (RS). Lead I is predominantly negative (net area -20) with an initial Q/QS. II, III and aVF are deep QS and the frontal axis is northwest, about -100. The spike looks double/notched in II, V1 and I (two components about 10-20 ms apart), consistent with a small V-V offset. A narrow paced QRS with R in V1, negative I and a northwest axis is the classic CRT pattern. Confident.
mimic-43155662.malfunction_evidence: Every spike is followed by a captured, consistent paced QRS. No pauses.
mimic-43155662.av_relationship: P-synchronous tracking: each small sinus P is followed by a ventricular spike after a short, fixed AV delay

mimic-43155662.notes: A good CRT example. The short paced QRS with RS in V1 contrasts well with an RV-paced LBBB pattern.
teaching_points: CRT pattern: paced QRS narrower than RV pacing, R in V1, negative lead I, northwest axis
A double or notched spike can reflect sequential LV and RV outputs (V-V offset)
Atrial-sensed BiV pacing with a short AV delay keeps pacing at close to 100% of beats

mimic-40832604.atrial_rhythm: Probable sinus tachycardia about 100 bpm. The P waves are low-amplitude and merge with the preceding T wave, seen as a hump starting about 150 ms before each spike in II.
mimic-40832604.mode: Probable DDD/VDD atrial-sensed (P-synchronous) ventricular pacing. The tracking is not proven because the P waves are hard to separate.
mimic-40832604.site_evidence: LBBB-like: deep QS in V1-V2, rS in V3 and transition at V4-V5. The frontal axis is inferior (about +65), with positive II, III and aVF and a negative aVL. Lead I is small and positive. Paced QRS about 120-140 ms. An LBBB pattern with an inferior axis points to an RV septal/outflow site, not the RV apex. The spike appears as a small biphasic artifact (about 10 ms between components). A CRT system with an anterior-vein LV lead cannot be fully excluded, but there is no R in V1 and lead I is not negative. Moderate confidence.
mimic-40832604.malfunction_evidence: All 17 beats are paced and captured at a constant RR of about 590 ms. No pauses and no non-capturing spikes.
mimic-40832604.av_relationship: Probably P-synchronous, with the P waves partly buried in the preceding T
mimic-40832604.beats: All ventricular paced, at about 0.31, 0.90, 1.49, 2.07, 2.65, 3.25 s and so on to about 9.7 s (RR about 590 ms). No intrinsic, fusion or PVC beats identified.
mimic-40832604.notes: The spikes are small but visible before every QRS on the zoom and in V3.
teaching_points: An LBBB-like paced QRS with an inferior axis (positive II, III, aVF) indicates an RV septal/outflow lead
Compare with RV apical pacing, which has a superior axis

mimic-43957157.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at about 54-55 bpm (lower rate). The paced P waves are low-amplitude. The last beat (about 9.07-9.27 s) appears to be a sensed sinus P, which inhibited the atrial output.
mimic-43957157.mode: DDD at the lower rate: atrial pacing followed by a ventricular output at a programmed AV delay of about 200 ms. Intrinsic AV conduction is about equal to the AV delay, so the ventricular output lands on the conducted QRS.
mimic-43957157.ventricular_site: Not truly paced: the QRS is intrinsically conducted (pseudofusion). Conduction-system pacing is a remote alternative.
mimic-43957157.site_evidence: The QRS is narrow (about 85-95 ms) and normal-looking in every beat: tall R in I, aVL and V4-V6, rS in V1, axis about -8. The ventricular spike in I, II and aVF falls exactly at QRS onset with no isoelectric latency and no change in morphology. That fits pseudofusion with an AV-conducted beat, not selective His capture.
mimic-43957157.malfunction: None. Pseudofusion is a functional finding (AV delay about equal to intrinsic PR), not a malfunction.
mimic-43957157.malfunction_evidence: The atrial spike (best seen in V1) is followed about 200 ms later by a small ventricular spike at the onset of a narrow QRS whose morphology is identical in every beat (for example, A spike at about 0.30 s, V spike/QRS at about 0.50-0.54 s).
mimic-43957157.av_relationship: AV sequential timing. The ventricles are actually activated by intrinsic conduction of the paced P (PR about 200 ms).
mimic-43957157.beats: Atrial-paced beats with pseudofused ventricular outputs at A spikes of about 0.30, 1.40, 2.50, 3.60, 4.70, 5.80, 6.90 and 8.00 s (QRS about 240 ms later). The last QRS at about 9.27 s follows a sensed P at about 9.07 s with no atrial spike.
mimic-43957157.rates: Lower rate about 54-55 bpm (A-A about 1100 ms)
mimic-43957157.notes: A useful example of a ventricular spike landing on a conducted QRS. It can prompt discussion of AV search/hysteresis or managed ventricular pacing to avoid unnecessary RV pacing.
teaching_points: When the programmed AV delay is about equal to native AV conduction, the V spike falls on an intrinsic QRS: pseudofusion
A narrow QRS with a spike at its onset is not capture; compare morphology with the native QRS
Atrial pacing at the lower rate followed by a narrow conducted QRS

mimic-47154469.atrial_rhythm: Uncertain. Low-amplitude positive humps after each T wave (about 400-450 ms after each spike, about 300 ms before the next spike) in III/aVF may be P waves, or may be the terminal part of a biphasic T. There is no convincing independent atrial activity.
mimic-47154469.mode: Regular ventricular pacing at about 79 bpm. If the humps are P waves, this is P-synchronous tracking with a long AV delay; otherwise VVI(R). Unclear.
mimic-47154469.site_evidence: LBBB-like: QS/W-shaped QS in V1 and deep QS in V2-V4, with a late transition (small R only in V5-V6). Lead I is negative and aVL is negative, and the inferior leads are positive. Frontal axis about +120 (right inferior). Paced QRS about 140-145 ms. A large, single spike. An LBBB pattern with an inferior-right axis and negative I/aVL fits an RVOT (free-wall or high-septal) site. Negative I and a right axis are also seen in CRT, but V1 has no R and the QRS is not narrow, so CRT is less likely. Moderate confidence.
mimic-47154469.malfunction_evidence: 13 consecutive captured paced beats at a constant interval of about 755 ms. No pauses or non-capturing spikes.
mimic-47154469.av_relationship: Uncertain. There is no clear dissociated P-wave activity marching through, and the possible P waves keep a fixed relationship to the paced beats.
mimic-47154469.beats: All ventricular paced, at about 0.35, 1.11, 1.87, 2.62, 3.38, 4.13, 4.88, 5.64, 6.39, 7.14, 7.90, 8.65 and 9.40 s. No intrinsic, fusion or PVC beats seen.
mimic-47154469.notes: Large unipolar-looking spikes make this a clean image. Atrial activity could not be resolved even with enlargement.
teaching_points: An LBBB-like paced QRS with an inferior axis and negative lead I/aVL suggests an RV outflow tract lead
Large spikes suggest unipolar pacing configuration

mimic-41873119.atrial_rhythm: Probable sinus rhythm about 83 bpm. The P waves are small and partly obscured by tremor/noise.
mimic-41873119.site_evidence: The QRS is about 90-100 ms with QS in V1-V2 (possible old anterior MI). It is upright in I, II and aVF and V4-V6, with an axis of about +40. The morphology is constant and no stimulus artifacts are seen in any lead or on the zoom.
mimic-41873119.malfunction_evidence: The machine's 'demand atrial pacing and ineffective stimuli' most likely comes from high-frequency muscle/tremor noise. No reproducible spikes are seen.
mimic-41873119.beats: All intrinsic, regular at RR about 720 ms (about 14 beats)
mimic-41873119.notes: Heavy baseline noise. Not useful for the pacing module.
teaching_points: Muscle tremor can trigger false pacer-spike detection by the ECG cart

mimic-44351423.atrial_rhythm: No organized P waves visible. Consistent with AF (as the machine states), though the quantized, stair-stepped signal limits assessment of fibrillatory waves.
mimic-44351423.mode: Ventricular pacing at a fixed rate of about 71-72 bpm without atrial tracking (VVI(R) behaviour in AF)
mimic-44351423.ventricular_site: Biventricular (CRT), probable. LV-only is the main alternative.
mimic-44351423.site_evidence: V1-V2 show an upright, dominant broad R (RBBB-like). Lead I is near-isoelectric to slightly negative (net -3.7). II, III and aVF are deep QS, with a northwest/superior axis of about -95. There is QS in V3-V6. The spike is a close double (two components about 15-20 ms apart in V4-V6 and I), suggesting two ventricular outputs with a small V-V offset. The paced QRS is wide, about 160-170 ms. An R in V1 with a negative/isoelectric I, a northwest axis and a double spike favours BiV. The wide QRS keeps LV-only capture (for example, loss of RV capture) in the differential. Moderate confidence.
mimic-44351423.malfunction_evidence: Every spike is followed by a consistent paced QRS at a constant interval of about 835 ms.
mimic-44351423.av_relationship: No visible atrial activity, so no AV relationship (AF)
mimic-44351423.beats: All ventricular paced, at about 0.22, 1.06, 1.89, 2.73, 3.56, 4.40, 5.23, 6.07, 6.90, 7.75, 8.6 and 9.45 s. No intrinsic or fusion beats seen.
mimic-44351423.notes: The recording is heavily quantized (stair-step artifact), which degrades fine detail. The double spikes are best seen in V4-V6.
teaching_points: An R in V1 with a negative lead I and a northwest axis in a paced rhythm suggests LV involvement (BiV or LV-only)
A double spike with a short separation suggests sequential LV and RV outputs
CRT pacing in AF runs without atrial tracking

mimic-47054689.atrial_rhythm: No clear P waves. The intrinsic RR is irregular (about 690-870 ms), favouring AF, but this is uncertain.
mimic-47054689.mode: Ventricular demand pacing (VVI) at a lower rate of about 70 bpm (escape about 850 ms), with intrinsic beats inhibiting output and several fusion/pseudofusion beats
mimic-47054689.site_evidence: Fully paced beats (for example, at 0.44 and 1.28 s) are LBBB-like: deep QS in V1 and QS in V2-V3. Lead I has a tall broad positive R. II, III and aVF are deep QS (superior axis about -60). Paced QRS about 150-160 ms. This is the classic RV apical pattern. Confident.
mimic-47054689.malfunction: None. Inhibition and escape timing are appropriate; the fusion beats are functional.
mimic-47054689.malfunction_evidence: Spikes occur about 850 ms after the last sensed or paced event (0.37, 1.22, 5.25, 6.11, 6.96, 7.82 s). Intrinsic beats arriving earlier inhibit output (2.78, 3.59, 4.40, 8.63, 9.40 s).

Fusion: about 6.11-6.17 s (spike followed by a narrower, notched QRS). Possible pseudofusion: about 2.07-2.09 s (narrow QRS with a notch at the time a spike was due). Intrinsic narrow: 2.78, 3.59, 4.40, 8.63, 9.40 s.
mimic-47054689.rates: Pacing interval about 850 ms (about 70 bpm). Intrinsic rate about 70-85 bpm, irregular.
mimic-47054689.notes: Competition between intrinsic conduction and the pacing rate gives a mix of paced, fused and native beats in one strip.
teaching_points: In demand pacing, intrinsic beats faster than the lower rate inhibit the pacemaker
When the intrinsic and pacing rates are close, fusion and pseudofusion beats appear
RV apical pacing: LBBB-like QRS, superior axis, positive lead I

mimic-46772727.atrial_rhythm: Atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular RR, fibrillatory baseline in V1, no P waves)
mimic-46772727.site_evidence: The conducted QRS is about 110-130 ms (IVCD) and identical in every beat, with rS/QS in V1, tall R in V4-V6 and low limb-lead voltage. The irregular rhythm with constant morphology and no stimulus artifacts rules against a paced rhythm.
mimic-46772727.malfunction_evidence: No spikes in any lead or on the zoom. The machine's 'A-V sequential pacing and ineffective stimuli' is a false detection from noise.
mimic-46772727.beats: All intrinsic. RR varies from about 500 to 900 ms (about 14 beats).
mimic-46772727.notes: A false pacer detection by the cart.

mimic-49254122.atrial_rhythm: No clear P waves. Intrinsic RR is irregular (about 700-900 ms), probably AF, uncertain.
mimic-49254122.mode: Ventricular demand pacing (VVI) at a lower rate of about 63 bpm (escape about 940-950 ms), with normal inhibition by intrinsic beats
mimic-49254122.site_evidence: Paced beats (4.60-6.50 s) are LBBB-like: small QS in V1 and deep QS in V2-V4. aVF is deep QS and aVL and aVR are positive, giving a superior axis of about -70 to -90. Lead I could not be seen during paced beats (column 1 shows only intrinsic beats). Paced QRS is clearly wide (about 150 ms) compared with the native 90 ms. QS in V4 and a superior axis fit RV apical pacing.
mimic-49254122.malfunction: None. Spikes come at the escape interval after the last sensed beat, so sensing is appropriate.
mimic-49254122.malfunction_evidence: Spike at 3.68 s, 935 ms after the intrinsic beat at 2.74 s; then paced at 4.60, 5.55, 6.50, 7.47 s (about 950 ms apart). Intrinsic beats at 8.29 and 9.19 s inhibit pacing.
mimic-49254122.beats: Intrinsic narrow: 0.40, 1.19, 2.04, 2.74, 8.29, 9.19 s. Spike with fusion/pseudofusion (narrow QRS just after the spike): 3.68 s. Fully paced: 4.60, 5.55, 6.50 s. Paced, possibly partly fused: 7.47 s. PVC: 9.73 s (wide, tall broad R in V1, negative in II).
mimic-49254122.rates: Pacing about 63 bpm. Intrinsic rate about 70-85 bpm, irregular.
mimic-49254122.notes: A good strip showing demand behaviour: pacing takes over when the intrinsic rate slows below the lower rate, and native beats return later.
teaching_points: Demand pacing: output only when no intrinsic event occurs within the escape interval
The beat at the transition is often fused or pseudofused
RV apical paced morphology: LBBB-like with a superior axis

mimic-46225619.atrial_rhythm: Probable sinus rhythm about 70 bpm. A small P-like deflection is seen about 130 ms before each ventricular spike in V1/II, but low amplitude and noise make this uncertain.
mimic-46225619.mode: Probable DDD/VDD atrial-sensed biventricular pacing. VVI cannot be excluded.
mimic-46225619.ventricular_site: Biventricular (CRT), probable. LV-only is the main alternative.
mimic-46225619.site_evidence: V1 shows a dominant monophasic R (RBBB-like) and V2 an RS. Lead I is negative (QS-like). II, III and aVF are deep QS, aVR is tall positive, and the frontal axis is northwest (about -108). There is QS in V3-V6. Paced QRS is wide, about 170 ms, with a slurred onset. R in V1, negative I and a northwest axis are the classic BiV pattern. The deep inferior QS points to an RV-apical contribution, because LV-only lateral-vein pacing usually gives a right-inferior axis. The very wide QRS and slurred onset keep LV-only (loss of RV capture) in the differential. The spike is biphasic, with a possible second component about 10 ms later. Moderate confidence.
mimic-46225619.malfunction_evidence: Every spike is followed by an identical paced QRS at a constant interval of about 857 ms.
mimic-46225619.av_relationship: Probably P-synchronous, with P about 130 ms before each spike. Uncertain.
mimic-46225619.beats: All ventricular paced, at about 0.31, 1.19, 2.03, 2.89, 3.74, 4.59, 5.44, 6.30, 7.16, 8.03, 8.90 and 9.78 s. No intrinsic, fusion or PVC beats.
mimic-46225619.notes: A useful contrast case: a CRT-pattern frontal axis with a wide paced QRS. A teaching question could be BiV vs LV-only.
teaching_points: A dominant R in V1 with a negative lead I and a northwest axis means the LV is being paced
A very wide paced QRS with an R in V1 should prompt a check of RV capture (LV-only vs BiV)

ptbxl-5547.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at 60/min. Every atrial spike is followed by a small upright P wave in II and aVF, so the atrium is captured.
ptbxl-5547.av_relationship: AV sequential. Each atrial spike is followed by a ventricular spike about 230-235 ms later, a long AV delay (machine: PROAV). No intrinsic conduction and no fusion in 10 s.
ptbxl-5547.mode: DDD, AV sequential pacing at the lower rate (A-A 1.00 s)
ptbxl-5547.site_evidence: The paced QRS is very wide (about 200-220 ms). Lead I and aVL are upright. II, III and aVF show deep QS, giving a left superior axis. V1-V3 are QS, V4 is rS/QS, and V5-V6 are small and fragmented. There is no R in V1 and lead I is positive, which rules out LV-only and biventricular pacing. This is a textbook RV apical (LBBB-like, superior axis) pattern.
ptbxl-5547.malfunction_evidence: Every atrial spike captures the atrium and every ventricular spike captures the ventricle. There are no pauses and no inappropriate spikes.
ptbxl-5547.beats: Ten AV-paced beats. Atrial spikes at about 0.40, 1.40, 2.40 ... 9.40 s; ventricular spikes at about 0.62, 1.62 ... 9.62 s. No intrinsic, fused, pseudofused or premature beats.
ptbxl-5547.rates: Atrial-paced rate 60/min (lower rate). AV interval about 230 ms. Ventricular-paced rate 60/min.
ptbxl-5547.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Large ventricular spikes suggest unipolar ventricular pacing. Same age and sex (49 F) and the same report template as ptbxl-15241 and ptbxl-9182, so possibly the same patient on different dates. Clean example for showing both spikes, P capture and RV apical morphology.
teaching_points: Two spikes per beat: atrial spike, P wave, then ventricular spike and wide QRS = AV sequential (DDD) pacing.
RV apical capture: LBBB-like QS in V1, upright I and aVL, negative II/III/aVF (left superior axis).
Without an R in V1 and with lead I positive, LV-only and biventricular (CRT) pacing are excluded.
The AV delay is measured spike to spike (about 230 ms here).

ptbxl-15241.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at 70/min (A-A 0.86 s). After each atrial spike there is only a tiny, barely visible P wave. Capture is likely because the QRS follows each atrial spike at a fixed interval.
ptbxl-15241.av_relationship: AV sequential timing. The ventricular spike comes about 185-190 ms after the atrial spike, and the ventricular complex starts 10-20 ms after it.
ptbxl-15241.site_evidence: The complexes after the ventricular spike are narrow, about 85-90 ms. Lead I and aVL are upright, II is upright with a terminal negative part, aVF ends negative, V1-V3 are deep narrow QS, and V5 has a tall R. A pure RV-paced QRS cannot be this narrow. The pattern looks like a blend of the patient's own conduction and RV capture: in ptbxl-9182 (likely the same 49 F patient) the fusion beats look like this, and the pure intrinsic and pure paced beats look different. It is not conduction-system pacing: there is no isoelectric spike-to-QRS latency, and the era argues against it. It is not biventricular: there is no R in V1.
ptbxl-15241.malfunction_evidence: There is no pause, no spike without a response and no misplaced spike. The narrow complexes come from timing (programmed AV delay about equal to the patient's own AV conduction time), not from device failure.
ptbxl-15241.beats: Twelve beats, all alike. Atrial spikes at about 0.22, 1.08, 1.94, 2.80 ... 9.68 s. Ventricular spikes about 0.19 s later (0.41, 1.27, 2.13 ...). Every ventricular complex is a consistent fusion beat, possibly pseudofusion.
ptbxl-15241.rates: Atrial-paced 70/min. AV interval (spike to spike) about 185-190 ms. Ventricular complexes about 85-90 ms.
ptbxl-15241.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. The machine read AVDPR. If a reader compares this with the fully paced complexes of ptbxl-5547 or ptbxl-9182, the point becomes clear. Without a comparison tracing it is subtle; it could be mistaken for His pacing or for failed capture.
teaching_points: A narrow QRS right after a ventricular spike is not normal RV capture. Think fusion or pseudofusion first.
Consistent fusion happens when the programmed AV delay roughly equals the patient's own AR/PR conduction time.
Fusion is a timing effect, not a malfunction. Shortening the AV delay or using AV search hysteresis changes it.
A narrow paced QRS in a 1990s device is not conduction-system or CRT pacing; check the spike-to-QRS latency and V1.

ptbxl-21193.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at 72/min (A-A 0.84 s). The P wave after each atrial spike is low in amplitude but present in II.
ptbxl-21193.av_relationship: AV sequential. Atrial spike to ventricular spike is about 175-180 ms. No intrinsic or fused beats.
ptbxl-21193.site_evidence: The paced QRS is very wide (about 200 ms; machine 232 ms). II, III and aVF are QS (superior axis), aVR and aVL are upright, and lead I is small and negative-then-positive, nearly isoelectric (axis about -90 deg). V1 has a small broad initial r and then a deep S. V2-V6 are all negative (QS), so the precordial leads are negatively concordant. V1 has no dominant R, and the QRS is far too wide and LBBB-like for biventricular pacing. A negative or isoelectric lead I is a known variant of RV apical pacing.
ptbxl-21193.malfunction_evidence: All atrial and ventricular spikes capture at regular intervals.
ptbxl-21193.beats: Twelve AV-paced beats. Atrial spikes at about 0.28, 1.11, 1.95 ... 9.49 s; ventricular spikes about 0.18 s later (0.46, 1.29 ... 9.66 s).
ptbxl-21193.rates: 72/min AV sequential. AV interval about 175-180 ms.
ptbxl-21193.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Large spikes (unipolar). Good distractor case: lead I is negative or isoelectric, but V1 is not R-dominant, so this is not CRT or LV pacing.
teaching_points: DDD AV sequential pacing: atrial spike, small P, then ventricular spike and wide QRS.
A negative or isoelectric lead I alone does not prove LV or biventricular capture. Check V1: BiV and LV pacing usually show an R or Rs in V1; here V1 is mainly negative.
Negative concordance V2-V6 with a superior axis fits apical RV pacing.

ptbxl-15444.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm at about 80/min with small P waves, plus one early beat (machine: PAC).
ptbxl-15444.av_relationship: P-synchronous. Each paced QRS follows a sinus P at a fixed short sensed AV delay (P onset to spike about 110-130 ms). The paced rate varies with the sinus rate (V-V 0.70-0.75 s).
ptbxl-15444.site_evidence: The paced QRS is about 150-160 ms. Lead I and aVL are upright, II, III and aVF are deep QS (left superior axis), V1-V4 are QS, V5 is rS and V6 is a small rs. There is no R in V1 and lead I is positive, which excludes LV-only and biventricular pacing.
ptbxl-15444.malfunction_evidence: The early complex at about 0.82 s is sensed and inhibits ventricular output. The sinus P that falls in its T wave (refractory period/PVARP) is not tracked. Tracking resumes with the next P (spike at 1.83 s).
ptbxl-15444.beats: Paced beats (sinus P, then ventricular spike) at about 0.29, 1.83, 2.54, 3.28, 4.05, 4.78, 5.53, 6.27, 7.02, 7.75, 8.50 and 9.22 s. At about 0.82 s there is an early non-paced complex with no spike: about 80-90 ms, I upright, II/aVF negative, V1 upright R (RBBB/left-axis pattern). It is probably a conducted PAC with aberration (as the machine reads it), though a fascicular PVC cannot be excluded. No atrial spikes.
ptbxl-15444.rates: Sinus and paced rate about 81/min. Sensed AV delay about 110-130 ms from P onset.
ptbxl-15444.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Muscle tremor in the limb leads. Spike amplitude varies between leads (small in II on some beats), so look in aVR/aVL and V1-V6 as well.
teaching_points: VDD/DDD tracking: every paced QRS is preceded by a sinus P at a constant short interval, and the paced rate follows the sinus rate.
No atrial spikes: the atrium is sensed, not paced.
An early intrinsic beat inhibits ventricular output, and a P wave inside the refractory period/PVARP is not tracked.
RV apical paced morphology: QS in V1, left superior axis.

ptbxl-21817.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at about 55/min (A-A 1.09 s). The P waves after the atrial spikes are very low in amplitude. The QRS follows each atrial spike at a fixed interval, so capture is likely.
ptbxl-21817.av_relationship: The paced P conducts on its own: atrial spike to QRS onset is about 200-210 ms. The ventricular spike is delivered at about 225-230 ms, roughly 20-25 ms after the native QRS has already started.
ptbxl-21817.mode: DDD with AV sequential timing and intrinsic AV conduction
ptbxl-21817.site_evidence: No complex is captured by the ventricle. Each QRS is native: narrow (about 80-90 ms) with tall voltage in V2-V5. Each ventricular spike sits on the upstroke of the R wave and leaves the QRS shape unchanged, which is pseudofusion. The pacing site cannot be judged.
ptbxl-21817.malfunction_evidence: Pseudofusion is a timing effect: the programmed AV delay is about equal to the native AR interval, and the RV lead senses the local signal after the surface QRS has begun. A spike 20-25 ms into the QRS is not undersensing.
ptbxl-21817.beats: Nine beats, all the same pattern: atrial spike, low P, native narrow QRS, and a ventricular spike about 20-25 ms after QRS onset (pseudofusion). Atrial spikes at about 0.59, 1.69, 2.78, 3.88, 4.97, 6.06, 7.15, 8.25 and 9.34 s; ventricular spikes at about 0.82, 1.92, 3.01, 4.11, 5.20, 6.29, 7.39, 8.49 and 9.57 s.
ptbxl-21817.rates: Atrial-paced 55/min. AR about 200-210 ms. Programmed AV delay about 225-230 ms (spike to spike).
ptbxl-21817.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. The machine read is APR FREQ VPCX with LVH voltage; the large spikes may inflate the measured voltage. Seen best at high paper speed: the R upstroke begins before the ventricular spike.
teaching_points: Pseudofusion: a pacing spike falls inside a native QRS whose shape is unchanged; the spike has no effect.
It happens when the AV delay is about the same as the patient's own AR conduction. It is not loss of capture and not undersensing.
Compare with AAI pacing: here a second (ventricular) spike is buried in every QRS.

ptbxl-5136.atrial_rhythm: Atrial fibrillation (fine f waves, no P waves, irregular intrinsic RR intervals).
ptbxl-5136.av_relationship: AF with variable conduction. Intrinsic QRS shows RBBB with LVH voltage.
ptbxl-5136.mode: VVI demand pacing (lower rate interval about 0.85 s, 70/min) with normal inhibition by conducted beats
ptbxl-5136.site_evidence: Judged from the fully paced beats at 6.78 and 7.63 s. QRS about 140 ms. Lead I is low and broadly upright, aVL is upright, II and aVF are deep QS, V1 is small and mainly negative, V3-V5 are deep QS and V6 is QS. This is an LBBB-like pattern with a left superior axis. There is no R in V1 (unlike the patient's own RBBB beats), so it is not LV-only or biventricular pacing.
ptbxl-5136.malfunction_evidence: Spikes at 2.22, 5.06 and 8.48 s fall 30-50 ms after the start of a native RBBB QRS and do not change it (pseudofusion). In RBBB the right ventricle is activated late, so the RV lead senses late and the device paces before sensing. This is not true undersensing. Pacing intervals are consistent: 0.85 s paced to paced, 0.87-0.90 s from native QRS onset.
ptbxl-5136.beats: Fusion or pseudofusion at 0.65 s. Intrinsic at 1.35 s. Pseudofusion at 2.22 s. PVC at 2.61 s (no spike; V1 tall broad R, deep negative lead I, LV origin). Intrinsic at 3.36 and 4.19 s. Pseudofusion at 5.06 s. Intrinsic at 5.88 s. Fully paced at 6.78 and 7.63 s. Pseudofusion at 8.48 s. Intrinsic at 9.09 and 9.79 s.
ptbxl-5136.rates: Lower rate about 70/min (0.85 s). Intrinsic AF rate about 70-100/min.
ptbxl-5136.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. VVI_AF is an acceptable alternative answer. The case shows the full range in one strip: native RBBB beats, pseudofusion, fully paced beats and a PVC.
teaching_points: In AF the ventricular pacemaker paces only when the RR interval exceeds the lower rate interval.
Pseudofusion: a spike inside an unchanged native QRS. With RBBB the RV lead senses late, so the spike can land well into the surface QRS without being undersensing.
The paced complexes (LBBB-like, superior axis) differ from the native RBBB complexes; compare V1 between the two.

ptbxl-382.atrial_rhythm: Atrial fibrillation (irregular RR intervals, no P waves).
ptbxl-382.av_relationship: AF with variable conduction and narrow native QRS.
ptbxl-382.mode: VVI demand pacing (lower rate interval about 0.86 s, 70/min); mostly inhibited by native beats
ptbxl-382.site_evidence: There is no fully paced complex. All three spike-bearing beats are fusion beats with mostly native narrow morphology. The 9.15 s beat starts with a small negative wave in II and has an altered, broad upright T, which suggests a minor RV contribution, but the site cannot be judged.
ptbxl-382.malfunction_evidence: Spikes appear only when the RR interval reaches about 0.86 s (0.27, 7.55 and 9.15 s). Each is followed within 0-60 ms by a native QRS, giving fusion. No spike is delivered too early, and none is clearly missing.
ptbxl-382.beats: Fusion at about 0.27 s (the QRS starts at the spike; lead I differs from native beats). Native AF beats at 1.11, 1.77, 2.39, 2.98, 3.71, 4.52, 5.20, 5.89, 6.70 and 8.29 s. Fusion at 7.55 s (spike about 25 ms before a mostly native QRS). Fusion at 9.15 s (spike about 60 ms before the native R, with an altered terminal QRS and T).
ptbxl-382.rates: Escape interval about 0.86 s (70/min). AF ventricular response about 70-100/min.
ptbxl-382.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Baseline drift and tremor. Lead V6 looks time-shifted on the last beat, probably a recording artefact. Teaching use is limited because no complex is fully paced; FUSION is an alternative answer.
teaching_points: In AF a VVI pacemaker paces only when a pause exceeds the lower rate interval.
When a native beat arrives at the same moment, the result is a fusion beat whose shape lies between paced and native.

ptbxl-5544.atrial_rhythm: Cannot be determined. Heavy muscle tremor hides any P waves. Subtracting the paced QRS-T complexes did not reveal a consistent P wave rhythm. The machine's 'sinus rhythm + complete heart block' read could not be confirmed.
ptbxl-5544.av_relationship: No native conduction seen; every beat is paced. AV dissociation is possible but not demonstrated.
ptbxl-5544.mode: VVI at a fixed 70/min (lower rate interval 0.86 s). No atrial spikes. Sensing cannot be tested because there are no native beats.
ptbxl-5544.site_evidence: Paced QRS about 160 ms. Lead I and aVL are upright, II, III and aVF are deep QS (left superior axis), V1 is a small QS, V2-V5 are deep QS and V6 is rS. There is no R in V1, so it is not LV-only or biventricular pacing.
ptbxl-5544.malfunction_evidence: Every spike captures at a regular interval. No pauses.
ptbxl-5544.beats: Twelve ventricular-paced beats at about 0.30, 1.16, 2.01, 2.88, 3.74, 4.60, 5.46, 6.32, 7.18, 8.04, 8.90 and 9.76 s. No native beats, PVCs or fusion.
ptbxl-5544.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. VVI_CHB would be the answer only if dissociated P waves were visible; they are not, because of the noise. Large spikes.
teaching_points: Fixed-rate ventricular pacing with RV apical morphology: LBBB-like with a superior axis.
Do not call complete heart block unless dissociated P waves can actually be seen; here noise hides atrial activity.

ptbxl-7783.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm at about 88-95/min. After each PVC there is one atrial-paced beat.
ptbxl-7783.av_relationship: 1:1 native conduction with PR about 150 ms. The paced P conducts on its own: atrial spike to QRS onset about 200 ms. No ventricular pacing.
ptbxl-7783.mode: Dual-chamber device (DDD/DDI) with ventricular-based timing. The device is inhibited during sinus rhythm. After each sensed PVC the VA interval (about 0.65 s) runs out and the atrium is paced, then conducts normally (AAI-like behaviour).
ptbxl-7783.site_evidence: No ventricular pacing. The native QRS shows LAFB (rS in II/III/aVF) and QS in V1-V3 (old anteroseptal MI). PVCs: upright in II, III and aVF, negative in I, R in V1 (LV outflow-type origin).
ptbxl-7783.malfunction_evidence: Spikes occur only 0.64-0.68 s after each PVC, as expected for atrial escape timing after a sensed PVC. Each spike is followed by a low P and a native QRS that arrives earlier than the next sinus beat would have. A ventricular spike failing to capture is less likely: it would require a 92/min ventricular escape rate and three consecutive failures. The P wave after the spike is subtle, so this remains an interpretation.
ptbxl-7783.beats: Native sinus beats at about 0.31, 2.35, 3.03, 3.73, 4.41, 6.48, 7.16, 7.84 and 8.50 s. PVCs at 0.70, 4.76 and 8.89 s. Atrial spikes at 1.34, 5.44 and 9.54 s, each followed by a low P and a native narrow QRS at about 1.54, 5.64 and 9.74 s.
ptbxl-7783.rates: Sinus about 90/min. VA (atrial escape) interval after a PVC about 0.65 s. Atrial spike to QRS about 200 ms.
ptbxl-7783.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. The pacing behaviour is subtle and needs timing analysis. PACED_PVC is an alternative answer. Ventricular pacing is not shown.
teaching_points: A PVC resets dual-chamber timing. The next event can be an atrial-paced beat at the end of the VA interval.
An atrial spike followed by a small P and a native QRS means atrial pacing with the patient's own AV conduction.
A pacemaker that is mostly inhibited in sinus rhythm appears only after pauses.

ptbxl-18903.atrial_rhythm: Sinus bradycardia at about 58-62/min. P waves are clearly seen from about 3.3 s onward. No P waves are visible before the first three paced beats: the sinus was slower there, or the P waves are buried.
ptbxl-18903.av_relationship: Native conduction with PR about 170-200 ms and RBBB. Ventricular pacing is not linked to the P waves (no tracking), so the device competes with the sinus rhythm.
ptbxl-18903.mode: VVI demand pacing, lower rate interval about 1.07 s (56/min)
ptbxl-18903.site_evidence: Paced QRS about 180 ms. Lead I is upright and notched, aVL is upright, II, III and aVF are deep QS (left superior axis), V1 is a small rS/QS, V4-V5 are deep QS and V6 is rS. Native beats show RBBB (V1 rsR') with probable LAFB. The paced beats have no R in V1, so they are not LV-only or biventricular.
ptbxl-18903.malfunction_evidence: Paced intervals are consistent (1.05-1.08 s). Native beats arriving before the lower rate interval inhibit and reset the timing. Spikes inside QRS complexes are fusion or pseudofusion, not undersensing.
ptbxl-18903.beats: Fully paced at 0.24, 1.33 and 2.39 s. Mostly paced, possibly with slight fusion, at 3.46 s (sinus P about 140 ms before the spike). Native RBBB beats at 4.44, 5.43 and 6.40 s. Fusion at 7.48 s (V4-V5 show an R then S, between the paced and native shapes). Fully paced at 8.53 s. Near-pseudofusion at 9.61 s (QRS starts about 15 ms before the spike; V1 shows the native RBBB R').
ptbxl-18903.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Clean recording. One strip shows the whole range from fully paced, through fusion and pseudofusion, to native RBBB beats, because the sinus rate is close to the lower rate.
teaching_points: When the sinus rate is close to the VVI lower rate, paced, fused and native beats alternate.
Fusion beats have a shape between the paced (LBBB-like, superior axis) and native (RBBB) complexes.
Pseudofusion: the QRS has already started when the spike falls, so the spike changes nothing.
The native RBBB with left axis (bifascicular block) is likely the reason for the pacemaker.

ptbxl-21408.atrial_rhythm: Atrial paced at about 69/min (A-A 0.86 s). One sinus P at about 6.88 s inhibits the atrial output, so atrial sensing works. The P waves after atrial spikes are low in amplitude.
ptbxl-21408.av_relationship: Native AV conduction after each atrial spike: spike to QRS about 220-270 ms (first-degree AV delay). The sinus beat conducts with PR about 170-190 ms.
ptbxl-21408.mode: AAI (or DDD with an AV delay longer than the patient's own AR). There are no ventricular spikes.
ptbxl-21408.site_evidence: No ventricular pacing. The wide QRS (about 130 ms) is native LBBB: lead I has a tall monophasic R, aVL R, V1 QS and tall R in V5-V6. It is identical in the sinus-conducted beat at 7.05 s, which has no spike, so it is not a paced QRS.
ptbxl-21408.malfunction_evidence: Every atrial spike is followed by a conducted QRS. The sinus P at about 6.88 s correctly inhibits the atrial output, and timing restarts from it (next spike at 7.79 s).
ptbxl-21408.beats: Atrial spikes at about 0.72, 1.60, 2.45, 3.33, 4.22, 5.12, 6.00, 7.79, 8.71 and 9.56 s, each followed by a native LBBB QRS 220-270 ms later. A sinus-conducted beat without a spike at about 7.05 s. The first QRS at about 0.10 s belongs to a beat that started before the recording.
ptbxl-21408.rates: Atrial-paced about 69/min. Ventricular rate about 69/min. The machine HR of 130 is wrong; it counts the spikes as beats.
ptbxl-21408.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Good trap: the wide QRS after a spike looks like ventricular pacing, but the spike is atrial and the QRS is native LBBB.
teaching_points: A spike followed by a P wave, then a native QRS after a normal or long PR, is atrial pacing with native conduction (AAI behaviour).
A wide QRS after an atrial spike can be the patient's own bundle branch block. Compare with a non-paced sinus beat.
A sinus P that comes before the atrial escape interval inhibits atrial pacing (normal atrial sensing).

ptbxl-8013.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm at about 74/min with first-degree AV block (PR about 230-240 ms) and frequent PACs (4 in 10 s).
ptbxl-8013.mode: VVI demand pacing, lower rate interval about 0.97-1.0 s (60/min)
ptbxl-8013.site_evidence: No fully captured paced complex. Every spike-bearing QRS is narrow and matches the native QRS (QS V1-V3, old anteroseptal MI). The spikes fall about 10-20 ms before or at QRS onset, which is pseudofusion. The pacing site cannot be judged.
ptbxl-8013.malfunction_evidence: A spike appears only when the RR interval after a PAC reaches about 0.97-0.99 s. That interval (pause after the PAC plus the long PR) happens to equal the lower rate interval, so the spike lands on the conducted QRS. This is normal behaviour, not undersensing.
ptbxl-8013.beats: Sinus beats at about 0.03, 0.85, 3.14, 3.95, 6.20 and 8.44 s. PACs at 1.30, 4.40, 6.63 and 8.87 s. Pseudofusion beats (sinus P, long PR, ventricular spike at the onset of the native QRS) at 2.30, 5.39, 7.62 and 9.83 s, each 0.97-0.99 s after a PAC.
ptbxl-8013.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Clean tracing. The report says 'sinus beats, atrial premature beats and paced beats', but no beat is truly paced; all four spike beats are pseudofusion.
teaching_points: Pseudofusion: a ventricular spike falls at the start of a native QRS and leaves it unchanged.
It is triggered here by the pause after each PAC plus a long PR, which together equal the lower rate interval.
A spike inside a QRS is not automatically undersensing; check the timing against the lower rate.

ptbxl-9182.atrial_rhythm: Not clearly identifiable. No definite P waves before native or paced beats, and the native RR intervals are irregular. AF or atrial standstill is possible but not confirmed.
ptbxl-9182.av_relationship: Native narrow beats compete with ventricular pacing. There are no atrial spikes and no P-synchronous pacing.
ptbxl-9182.mode: VVI demand pacing, lower rate interval 0.86 s (70/min), no hysteresis
ptbxl-9182.site_evidence: Paced QRS about 180-200 ms. Lead I has an upright R, aVL a tall R, II, III and aVF are deep QS (left superior axis), V1 is a low-amplitude QS, V2-V5 are QS and V6 is small and notched. There is no R in V1, so it is not LV-only or biventricular. Native beats are narrow (about 70-80 ms) with high voltage in V4-V5.
ptbxl-9182.malfunction_evidence: Native beats inhibit pacing and reset the timing. The next spike comes exactly 0.86 s after each sensed beat (3.82 to 4.70 s, 5.50 to 6.40 s, 8.73 to 9.60 s).
ptbxl-9182.beats: Fully paced at 0.66, 1.52, 2.38 and 3.24 s. At 3.82 s a non-paced early complex with no spike (about 100 ms, I upright, II/aVF negative, V1 rSR'), probably a PVC. Fusion at 4.70 s. Native narrow beat at 5.50 s. Paced at 6.40 s. Fusion at 7.25 s. Native at 8.03 and 8.73 s. Paced at 9.60 s.
ptbxl-9182.rates: Lower rate 70/min (0.86 s). Native beats irregular, about 70-85/min.
ptbxl-9182.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. Probably the same patient (49 F) as ptbxl-5547 and ptbxl-15241. The fusion beats here look like the complexes in 15241. The machine read 'UR' (undetermined rhythm) and missed the pacing.
teaching_points: VVI demand pacing: a native beat inhibits output and restarts the lower rate interval.
Paced, fusion and native beats side by side make clear what a fusion beat looks like.
RV apical paced morphology compared with a narrow native QRS.

ptbxl-20768.atrial_rhythm: No organized P waves identified, even after subtracting the paced QRS-T complexes. The atrial rhythm is undetermined. No atrial spikes.
ptbxl-20768.av_relationship: No native conduction seen except the single non-paced complex. Atrial activity is not visible.
ptbxl-20768.mode: VVI at 72/min (lower rate interval about 0.84 s), inhibited and reset by one non-paced complex
ptbxl-20768.site_evidence: Paced QRS about 170-180 ms. Lead I and aVL are upright, II, III and aVF are QS (left superior axis), V1-V4 are deep QS, V5 is small and V6 has an upright notched R. There is no R in V1 and lead I is positive, which excludes LV-only and biventricular pacing.
ptbxl-20768.malfunction_evidence: The complex at 5.52 s inhibits ventricular output and resets the timing (next spike at 6.43 s). The slightly longer interval (0.91 s) fits late RV sensing of an LV-origin beat. All spikes capture.
ptbxl-20768.beats: Ventricular-paced at about 0.70, 1.54, 2.37, 3.21, 4.05 and 4.89 s. A non-paced complex at 5.52 s (about 100-110 ms, upright in I, rSR'/R in V1, tall R in V2-V3; probably a PVC of LV origin, as the machine reads it). Paced again at 6.43, 7.27, 8.10, 8.94 and 9.78 s (the recording ends just after the last spike).
ptbxl-20768.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. PACED_PVC is an alternative answer; the PVC shows normal ventricular sensing.
teaching_points: Classic RV apical paced pattern: QS in V1-V4, upright I and aVL, negative inferior leads.
A PVC is sensed, inhibits the next output and resets the lower rate timer.

ptbxl-16605.atrial_rhythm: Cannot be determined. V1 shows low-amplitude deflections between paced beats, but no consistent P wave rhythm can be confirmed. No atrial spikes.
ptbxl-16605.av_relationship: Every beat is ventricular paced. No native conduction.
ptbxl-16605.mode: VVI at a fixed 70/min (lower rate interval 0.86 s). Every beat is paced, so sensing cannot be tested.
ptbxl-16605.site_evidence: Paced QRS about 130-140 ms. Lead I is nearly isoelectric, aVL and aVR are upright and II, III and aVF are deep QS (axis about -90 deg). V1-V2 are low amplitude with no dominant R. V3-V6 are QS (negative concordance). The isoelectric lead I could raise the question of biventricular pacing, but V1 has no R or Rs, so RV apex is favoured. 1990s device, age 87.
ptbxl-16605.malfunction_evidence: Regular capture at every spike. No pauses.
ptbxl-16605.beats: Eleven ventricular-paced beats at about 0.77, 1.63, 2.49, 3.35, 4.21, 5.07, 5.93, 6.79, 7.65, 8.52 and 9.37 s. The sharp deflections in II, III and aVF at 0-0.05 s are a start-of-recording artefact, not spikes.
ptbxl-16605.notes: Confidence is on a 1-5 scale. The report says 'regular paced rhythm, apparently normal pacemaker function'. Tremor in the limb leads.
teaching_points: RV apical pacing can give a nearly isoelectric or negative lead I with a superior axis. V1 decides: no R in V1 argues against LV-only or biventricular (CRT) capture.
Negative concordance in V3-V6 is typical of apical pacing.

ptbxl-20050.atrial_rhythm: Sinus bradycardia with sinus arrhythmia (~50-55 bpm); upright P before each narrow QRS
ptbxl-20050.av_relationship: Sinus beats conducted 1:1 with normal PR; no atrial tracking. During the two paced beats no sinus P is clearly seen (sinus slowed or P hidden)
ptbxl-20050.beats: Sinus-conducted narrow QRS at ~0.78 and 1.63 s; ventricular paced (large spike + wide QRS) at 2.80 and 4.00 s; sinus-conducted again at ~5.20, 6.35, 7.43, 8.55, 9.72 s. No clear fusion, no PVCs (machine 'VPCX' = the paced beats)
ptbxl-20050.mode: VVI / ventricular demand pacing at ~50 bpm, inhibited by sinus beats
ptbxl-20050.site_evidence: Paced QRS LBBB-like: QS/rS in V1, QS in II and aVF (superior axis), positive in I and aVL; width ~140-160 ms
ptbxl-20050.malfunction_evidence: Paced at 2.80 s (1.17 s after the sinus beat at 1.63 s) and 4.00 s (1.20 s later); the sinus beat at 5.20 s comes before the next escape and inhibits. Every spike captures
ptbxl-20050.rates: Lower rate ~50 bpm (paced interval 1.20 s); sinus RR 1.08-1.17 s (~52-55 bpm)
teaching_points: Pacing appears only when sinus slows below the ~50 bpm lower rate
Escape interval after a sensed sinus beat equals the pacing interval (no hysteresis)
RV-apical paced QRS: LBBB-like with superior axis
Report and machine read missed the device (paced beats read as extrasystoles)
ptbxl-20050.notes: Original report does not mention a pacemaker, but two clear spikes with captured wide QRS are present.

ptbxl-14720.atrial_rhythm: Atrial fibrillation (irregularly irregular, no P waves)
ptbxl-14720.av_relationship: AF with variable AV conduction; no atrial tracking
ptbxl-14720.beats: Conducted narrow AF beats at ~0.58, 1.15, 1.74, 2.58, 3.26, 3.78, 4.37, 4.83, 6.42, 7.08, 7.55, 7.99, 8.59 s; ventricular paced at 5.67 and 9.44 s, each after an RR of ~0.85 s. The 5.67 s paced complex is smaller in II than the 9.44 s one (possible partial fusion)
ptbxl-14720.site_evidence: Paced QRS negative in II (superior axis), deep QS/W-shaped in V1-V3, negative in V4-V5, ~130-150 ms; lead I not recorded during a paced beat
ptbxl-14720.malfunction_evidence: Pacing only after RR reaches ~0.85 s (5.67, 9.44 s); the AF beat at 2.58 s arrived at 0.84 s, just before the escape interval, and inhibited
ptbxl-14720.rates: Lower rate ~70 bpm (escape 0.85 s); AF ventricular response RR 0.44-0.84 s
teaching_points: In AF a VVI pacemaker fires only after long RR intervals
The escape interval (~0.85 s) is the same after each paced beat
Mostly intrinsic rhythm: the pacemaker is a backup
