ptbxl-6596.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm at ~75-80 bpm, close to the pacing rate.
ptbxl-6596.av_relationship: Intrinsic AV conduction (PR ~0.17 s) on native beats; during paced stretches the P waves (where visible) sit at varying distances before the spikes (~0.27 down to ~0.1 s), i.e. not tracked. This is isorhythmic competition between the sinus node and the ventricular pacemaker.
ptbxl-6596.beats: Intrinsic narrow beat at ~0.43 s; V-paced beats at ~1.23, 2.05, 2.87, 3.68, 4.49, 5.31 s; intrinsic narrow beats at ~5.92 s (early, possibly a PAC) and ~6.68 s with no spike; fusion/pseudofusion at ~7.49 s (spike plus a near-native QRS); V-paced, probably partly fused, at ~8.31 and ~9.12 s.
ptbxl-6596.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~150-160 ms, LBBB-like: deep QS in V1-V3, broad R in I and aVL, negative III/aVF, near-isoelectric II, giving a left superior axis.
ptbxl-6596.malfunction_evidence: The escape interval after native beats (0.43->1.23 s, 6.68->7.49 s) equals the paced cycle (~0.81 s); native beats at 5.92 and 6.68 s inhibit pacing correctly; the 7.49 s spike falls at the onset of a native QRS exactly at the escape time (pseudofusion, not undersensing).
ptbxl-6596.rates: Lower rate ~74 bpm (0.81 s); sinus ~75-80 bpm; PR ~0.17 s.
teaching_points: Demand pacing: native beats inhibit the pacemaker and the next spike comes one escape interval later.
When the sinus rate is about the same as the lower rate, paced, fused and native beats alternate.
A spike at the start of a native QRS at the expected time is pseudofusion, a normal finding.
Native QRS (narrow) vs paced QRS (wide, QS V1-V3, left superior axis).
ptbxl-6596.notes: Machine 'SRTH FREQ VPCX PSVC'. Small humps before some paced beats may be P or T/U waves, so P tracking could not be shown. Alternative answer FUSION. 2 crops used.

ptbxl-20095.atrial_rhythm: Sinus bradycardia ~50-56 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia.
ptbxl-20095.av_relationship: Intrinsic AV conduction with PR ~0.15-0.18 s; ventricular spikes fall shortly after the P waves whenever the sinus cycle exceeds the escape interval (no tracking).
ptbxl-20095.beats: Intrinsic narrow beats at ~1.05, 7.00, 8.17, 9.27 s. V-paced fusion beats at ~2.22, 3.42, 4.61 s: spike after the P wave, QRS narrower than a pure paced beat but with negative III/aVF. Pseudofusion at ~5.81 s (spike at the onset of a native-looking QRS). No PVCs.
ptbxl-20095.site_evidence: Probable only: spiked complexes become QS in III/aVF with positive lead I (superior vector from the RV apex), but every paced beat is fused (QRS ~110-120 ms), so there is no pure paced complex to measure.
ptbxl-20095.malfunction_evidence: Spikes occur only after ~1.17-1.19 s without a sensed beat; native beats arriving at ~1.18 s cycles just beat the timer. The timing is borderline but consistent with normal sensing.
ptbxl-20095.rates: Lower rate ~50-51 bpm (escape ~1.18 s); sinus 50-56 bpm; PR ~0.16 s.
teaching_points: When the sinus rate hovers at the lower rate, you see a spectrum: native beats, fusion beats and pseudofusion.
A fusion beat has a spike and a QRS intermediate between native and paced; a pseudofusion beat has a spike over an unchanged native QRS.
Neither fusion nor pseudofusion is a malfunction: the spike is delivered on time.
Pacing at a lower rate of ~50 bpm backs up sinus bradycardia.
ptbxl-20095.notes: Machine 'SBRAD OCC VPCX PO IMI'. A clean tracing for teaching fusion. 1 crop used.

ptbxl-13588.atrial_rhythm: No P waves identifiable (possibly fine AF, or P waves hidden in the paced T waves).
ptbxl-13588.beats: Paced bigeminy: V-paced beats at ~0.38, 1.89, 3.42, 4.95, 6.48, 8.00, 9.53 s, each followed ~0.58-0.60 s later by a non-paced beat (~0.98, 2.49, 4.00, 5.53, 7.05, 8.58 s): QRS ~130-140 ms, rsR' in V1 (RBBB-like), negative II/III/aVF, positive I, fixed coupling, no preceding P.
ptbxl-13588.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~170 ms: deep QS in II/III/aVF (superior axis), positive aVR, small positive I, low-amplitude V1, QS in V3-V6.
ptbxl-13588.malfunction_evidence: Each non-paced beat is sensed and resets the timer: the next spike always follows 0.92 s later.
ptbxl-13588.rates: Escape/lower rate ~65 bpm (0.92 s); coupling 0.58-0.60 s; overall ventricular rate ~79 bpm.
teaching_points: Bigeminy in a paced rhythm: every paced beat is followed by an extrasystole at a fixed coupling interval.
The extrasystole is sensed and resets the VVI escape interval (constant 0.92 s), so pacing is normal.
An RBBB + left-axis extrasystole of ~130 ms without a P wave can be fascicular (left posterior fascicle) or aberrantly conducted supraventricular; the surface ECG may not settle it.
RV apical paced beats: superior axis, QS across V3-V6.
ptbxl-13588.notes: Machine reads PSVC BIGEM RBBB LAD3. The coupled beat lacks a visible P: either a fascicular-type PVC or a junctional/reciprocal supraventricular beat conducted with RBBB+LAFB. Fixed coupling to each paced beat suggests it is triggered by the paced beat. 1 crop used.

ptbxl-2090.atrial_rhythm: Not identifiable: no definite P waves (muscle-tremor noise in the limb leads); possible small P-like deflections ~0.3 s before some spikes, unconfirmed.
ptbxl-2090.beats: All 12 beats V-paced at a fixed cycle of ~0.83 s (spikes ~0.44, 1.28, 2.10, 2.94, 3.76, 4.60, 5.43, 6.25, 7.09, 7.92, 8.75, 9.58 s). No intrinsic, fused or premature beats.
ptbxl-2090.mode: VVI at ~72 bpm (tracking at a constant rate cannot be excluded because P waves are not visible)
ptbxl-2090.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~150-160 ms: lead I and aVL positive, deep QS in II/III/aVF (superior axis), small QS in V1, deep QS in V3-V5, small rS in V6.
ptbxl-2090.malfunction_evidence: Every spike captures and no pauses occur.
teaching_points: Regular ventricular paced rhythm: a spike before every wide QRS.
RV apical site: LBBB-like with a superior axis (negative II, III, aVF) and QS in the mid-precordial leads.
Varying spike height (e.g. tall in V1 at ~2.1 s) is a sampling effect, not an extra event.
ptbxl-2090.notes: The GE read missed the pacing (LVH statement); the report says regular paced rhythm with normal function. Tremor noise limits the atrial analysis. 1 crop used.

ptbxl-9032.atrial_rhythm: Sinus rhythm ~92 bpm (a P wave before every QRS).
ptbxl-9032.av_relationship: 1:1 intrinsic AV conduction (PR ~0.17-0.18 s); where spikes occur they come ~0.2 s after P onset, i.e. inside the early native QRS.
ptbxl-9032.beats: All QRS complexes are native and narrow (~100 ms). Large spikes sit at or just after QRS onset with an unchanged QRS (pseudofusion) at ~0.45, 1.78, 2.42, 3.04, 6.29, 6.96, 8.31, 9.00, 9.69 s; beats at ~1.11, 3.68, 4.31, 4.97, 5.64, 7.64 s have no spike. No captured paced beat, no PVCs.
ptbxl-9032.mode: Unclear. Most likely P-synchronous ventricular pacing (VDD/DDD) with an AV delay about equal to the native PR, causing pseudofusion; VVT (triggered) mode or ventricular undersensing are alternatives.
ptbxl-9032.site_evidence: No captured paced complex: every spiked QRS is identical to the native narrow QRS (V1 rS, I and II upright).
ptbxl-9032.malfunction_evidence: Spikes fall 10-20 ms after the native QRS onset with no change in QRS shape. That is pseudofusion, explained by the AV delay ending before the RV lead senses the native beat. True ventricular undersensing cannot be excluded without device data, so no malfunction is claimed.
ptbxl-9032.rates: Sinus ~92 bpm (RR 0.63-0.67 s); P-to-spike ~0.20 s; native PR ~0.17-0.18 s.
teaching_points: A spike inside an unchanged native QRS is pseudofusion: the spike is ineffective because the ventricle is already depolarising.
With intact AV conduction and an AV delay close to the PR interval, dual-chamber devices often produce pseudofusion.
Do not call undersensing until you have checked the timing (here the spikes are tied to the P waves, not random).
ptbxl-9032.notes: Machine read NSR LVH: the spikes were not recognised. The mechanism (DDD AV-delay pseudofusion vs VVT vs undersensing) is not provable from the surface ECG.

ptbxl-20693.atrial_rhythm: No P waves identified (possible AF or P waves not visible).
ptbxl-20693.av_relationship: No visible atrial activity; ventricular pacing at a fixed rate.
ptbxl-20693.beats: Spikes every ~0.835 s at ~0.24, 1.08, 1.91, 2.75, 3.59, 4.43, 5.27, 6.10, 6.94, 7.78 s. Beats 1-4 (0.24-2.75 s): spike at the onset of a narrow native QRS (I tall narrow R, V1 rS) = pseudofusion. Beats 5-10 (3.59-7.78 s): full capture with a wide RV-paced QRS. Non-paced beats at ~8.42, 9.05, 9.61 s (RR 0.64/0.63/0.56 s): RBBB-like (tall R in V1, narrow R plus S in V4-V6, deep T inversion), either a PVC triplet or aberrantly conducted beats; pacing is inhibited.
ptbxl-20693.site_evidence: Captured beats: QRS ~180 ms, deep QS in V1-V3, negative II/III/aVF (superior axis), positive I and aVL, QS in V4-V5, notched R in V6.
ptbxl-20693.malfunction_evidence: Pseudofusion beats occur exactly at the escape interval; the three faster non-paced beats correctly inhibit pacing (no spikes at 8.42-9.61 s).
ptbxl-20693.rates: Lower rate ~72 bpm (0.835 s); the late non-paced run ~95-107 bpm.
teaching_points: The same spike timing yields narrow pseudofusion beats when the native rhythm coincides and wide fully paced beats when it does not.
Pseudofusion: spike plus unchanged narrow QRS. Capture: spike plus wide LBBB-like superior-axis QRS.
Faster native or ectopic beats inhibit a VVI pacemaker completely.
RV apical capture: QS V1-V5 with a superior axis.
ptbxl-20693.notes: Machine 'VPR FREQ CSEC PVC'. The nature of the last three beats (PVC triplet vs rate-related RBBB aberrancy) is uncertain. Good side-by-side pseudofusion vs capture example. 1 crop used.

ptbxl-14854.atrial_rhythm: Probable sinus P waves, poorly seen in noise (machine: sinus rhythm with complete heart block).
ptbxl-14854.av_relationship: Probably dissociated: the P-to-spike interval seems to drift (~0.26 down to ~0.13 s over the first 5 s) without conduction, suggesting AV block; uncertain because of noise.
ptbxl-14854.beats: All 12 beats V-paced at a fixed cycle of ~0.86 s (~0.10, 0.96, 1.81, 2.68, 3.54, 4.39, 5.26, 6.12, 6.98, 7.83, 8.69, 9.56 s). No intrinsic, fused or premature beats.
ptbxl-14854.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~160 ms with a left superior axis (I and aVL positive, deep QS II/III/aVF) but an RBBB-like precordial pattern: small R in V1, tall R in V2, R/S in V3-V6. This is not the usual QS in V1-V3 of RV apical pacing. Positive V2-V3 raises the possibility of an LV/coronary-sinus lead, but the positive lead I is atypical for LV pacing; an RV apex with RBBB-pattern variant (or high V1/V2 placement) is also possible.
ptbxl-14854.malfunction_evidence: Every spike captures at a regular rate; no pauses or extra spikes.
ptbxl-14854.rates: Paced 70 bpm (0.86 s); atrial rate uncertain (~68-70 bpm).
teaching_points: An RBBB-like paced QRS (R in V1-V2) should prompt a check of lead position (lateral chest X-ray/echo): RV apex variant vs LV/coronary-sinus lead.
Noise can hide P waves; do not diagnose AV dissociation without clearly marching P waves.
Fixed-rate ventricular pacing with no visible atrial tracking suggests VVI.
ptbxl-14854.notes: Machine 'SRTH CHB VPR' (static_noise flag). If the P waves could be confirmed this would be VVI_CHB; if lead malposition were confirmed, LV_ONLY. Neither is provable on this tracing. 2 crops used.

ptbxl-7517.atrial_rhythm: sinus rhythm ~62 bpm, PR ~170 ms; one atrial-paced beat
ptbxl-7517.av_relationship: 1:1 intrinsic AV conduction (sinus and the atrial-paced beat both conduct with narrow QRS)
ptbxl-7517.beats: Beat 2: large spike at ~1.48 s with no preceding sinus P, followed by a small P and a narrow conducted QRS ~1.62 s (atrial paced, intrinsic conduction, no ventricular spike). All other beats (QRS ~0.63, 2.6, 3.54, 4.52, 5.49, 6.43, 7.35, 8.31, 9.29 s): sinus P, then a spike exactly at the onset of a narrow QRS whose V1 morphology matches beat 2 = ventricular pseudofusion. No fully paced wide QRS anywhere.
ptbxl-7517.mode: dual-chamber (DDD) most likely: atrial pacing at lower rate (~60 bpm, VA ~0.85 s) when sinus slows, and a ventricular spike at an AV delay (~170 ms) equal to the native PR, landing on the intrinsic QRS
ptbxl-7517.site_evidence: No captured paced ventricular complex; every ventricular spike is pseudofusion with a narrow (~80 ms) native QRS, so the lead position cannot be judged.
ptbxl-7517.malfunction_evidence: Pseudofusion is normal: the spike arrives before the RV lead senses a QRS that has already begun on the surface. Isolated sharp transient in V4 only at ~9.84 s, not seen in the simultaneous II/V1 strips and off the device timing, so probably artifact.
ptbxl-7517.rates: sinus ~62 bpm; atrial escape (VA) ~0.85 s (lower rate ~60); AV delay ~170 ms ~= native PR
teaching_points: A spike sitting on the start of a narrow QRS with unchanged morphology is pseudofusion, not loss of capture.
The one atrial-paced beat (1.48 s) conducts on its own: the device paces the atrium only when the sinus rate falls below the lower rate.
Pseudofusion in DDD means the programmed AV delay is about the same as the native PR; consider an AV-search or longer AV delay.
ptbxl-7517.notes: Machine read SRTH OCC APCX matches the atrial-paced beat. The spikes are large (probably unipolar). Whether the spikes on the sinus beats are ventricular (DDD) or R-triggered cannot be proven, but the timing (~170 ms after each sinus P) fits a DDD AV delay.

ptbxl-20051.av_relationship: AF with irregular intrinsic conduction (narrow QRS); no atrial tracking
ptbxl-20051.beats: Ventricular paced: 0.03, 3.54, 8.53 s. All other beats are intrinsic narrow AF-conducted: ~0.65, 1.29, 2.02, 2.73, 4.33, 4.97, 5.52, 6.25, 7.0, 7.74, 9.22, 9.82 s. No fusion, no PVCs.
ptbxl-20051.mode: VVI demand: pacing only after RR intervals reach the escape interval (~0.80 s); intrinsic RRs up to ~0.76 s inhibit
ptbxl-20051.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~170 ms. Lead I broad positive, aVL positive, II/III/aVF deeply negative (superior axis). V1 negative (QS-like, LBBB pattern); V4 QS and V5-V6 initially negative at 8.53 s.
ptbxl-20051.malfunction_evidence: Paced beats occur only after ~0.79-0.80 s pauses (2.73->3.54, 7.74->8.53 s); shorter intrinsic cycles are sensed and inhibit.
ptbxl-20051.rates: lower rate ~75 bpm (escape ~0.80 s); mean ventricular rate ~85 bpm
teaching_points: In AF a VVI device fires only when an RR interval reaches the escape interval (~800 ms here).
Paced beats are wide with an LBBB-like pattern and superior axis (RV apex); the conducted beats are narrow.
Intermittent pacing in AF is normal demand behaviour, not a malfunction.
ptbxl-20051.notes: VVI_DEMAND is an acceptable alternative answer. Machine read 'AFIB OCC VPCX' is correct.

ptbxl-15336.atrial_rhythm: no atrial activity visible (flat baseline; fine AF or atrial standstill possible)
ptbxl-15336.av_relationship: no P waves to relate; no atrial tracking or atrial spikes
ptbxl-15336.beats: Ventricular paced at 0.76, 1.63, 2.49, 3.34, 4.20, 5.07, 6.68, 7.53, 8.39, 9.25 s. One PVC at ~5.75 s (wide, upright in V1-V3 = RBBB-like, LV origin) inhibits pacing and resets the timer. No fusion.
ptbxl-15336.mode: VVI at ~70 bpm with normal sensing of the PVC
ptbxl-15336.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~200 ms. Lead I broad positive, aVL positive, II/III/aVF deep QS (superior axis). V1 QS/rS (LBBB-like); V4-V6 rS, predominantly negative.
ptbxl-15336.malfunction_evidence: After the PVC (~5.75 s) the next spike comes ~0.9 s later (6.68 s), about one escape interval, so the PVC was sensed.
teaching_points: This is the classic RV apical paced complex: LBBB-like V1, superior axis, positive lead I.
The PVC is upright in V1 and arises from the LV; it is sensed, and the pacing timer resets from it.
With no visible P waves the device works as VVI.
ptbxl-15336.notes: PACED_PVC is an alternative answer. There is a little high-frequency artifact in the first ~0.2 s.

ptbxl-8714.av_relationship: AF with fast irregular conduction; no atrial tracking
ptbxl-8714.beats: Intrinsic AF-conducted beats with LBBB-like wide QRS (~160 ms) at ~0.7, 1.35, 1.93, 2.4, 2.95, 3.58, 3.98, 6.38, 6.93, 7.63, 8.33, 9.1, 9.58 s. PVC couplet at ~4.43 and ~4.8 s (upright in V1, negative in III: RBBB-like, superior axis). One ventricular paced beat at 5.6 s after the post-couplet pause; possibly partly fused.
ptbxl-8714.mode: VVI demand backup (escape ~0.85 s, ~70 bpm); otherwise inhibited by the fast AF
ptbxl-8714.site_evidence: Only one paced beat, seen only in II/V1-V3 (lead I not recorded at 5.6 s). It is deeply negative in II (superior axis), low-amplitude in V1 and rS with a deep S in V3. Probable RV apex; low certainty.
ptbxl-8714.malfunction_evidence: The spike comes ~0.8-0.87 s after the second PVC, about the escape interval; intrinsic RRs up to ~0.78 s inhibit.
ptbxl-8714.rates: AF ventricular rate ~100 bpm; escape ~0.85 s (~70 bpm)
teaching_points: A single paced beat appears only after the compensatory pause following a PVC couplet.
In fast AF the VVI pacemaker stays inhibited almost all the time.
ptbxl-8714.notes: Lead I is low-voltage and noisy. VVI_AF is equally defensible. The report says 'one paced beat noted', which agrees.

ptbxl-4181.atrial_rhythm: sinus rhythm with mild sinus arrhythmia (~75-90 bpm)
ptbxl-4181.av_relationship: 1:1 conduction, PR ~200 ms (borderline first-degree AV block)
ptbxl-4181.beats: Every beat (~0.09, 0.78, 1.44, 2.27, 3.06, 3.85, 4.64, 5.39, 6.10, 6.79, 7.65, 8.45, 9.26 s) is a sinus-conducted narrow QRS (~90 ms) with a spike at or within ~10 ms of the surface QRS onset, before the main deflection. QRS morphology is unchanged, so these are pseudofusion or triggered spikes. No fully paced complex.
ptbxl-4181.mode: unclear: R-wave triggered (VVT) discharge, as the original report states, or atrial tracking with an AV delay equal to the native PR (pseudofusion); not separable on this tracing
ptbxl-4181.site_evidence: No captured paced QRS. Every spike sits on a narrow native QRS (positive in I, negative in III/aVF, rS in V1), so the lead position cannot be judged.
ptbxl-4181.malfunction_evidence: A spike falling inside a narrow intrinsic QRS is the expected behaviour of VVT, or pseudofusion; it is not loss of capture.
ptbxl-4181.rates: sinus ~79 bpm (RR 0.66-0.86 s); spike locked to every QRS onset
teaching_points: A spike on every native QRS with no change in QRS shape is pseudofusion or R-triggered (VVT) pacing, not failure to capture.
Triggered modes were used in older devices so that oversensing would never cause inhibition.
To tell triggered from tracking: in VVT the spike follows R-wave sensing; in DDD it follows the P wave at a fixed AV delay.
ptbxl-4181.notes: Baseline tremor artifact in the limb leads. The report says 'Eigenrhythmus mit R-getriggerter Pacerentladung'. The machine read ASVPR PROAV assumes atrial tracking. The spike is barely visible in aVF.

ptbxl-7204.atrial_rhythm: not clearly visible; small irregular baseline deflections could be dissociated P waves (machine read CHB) but are not convincing
ptbxl-7204.av_relationship: unclear; no fixed P-to-spike relation, so no atrial tracking
ptbxl-7204.beats: All 12 beats are ventricular paced at a fixed 0.8 s interval (spikes ~0.49, 1.29, 2.09, 2.89, 3.69, 4.47, 5.27, 6.07, 6.87, 7.66, 8.45, 9.25 s). No intrinsic, fusion or PVC beats.
ptbxl-7204.mode: VVI (fixed-rate pacing at ~75 bpm; sensing not testable)
ptbxl-7204.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~160 ms. II/III/aVF deep QS (superior axis); aVL and aVR positive; lead I small positive. V1 rS with deep S (LBBB-like); V4-V6 rS/negative. V2 has an unusually prominent R; probable RV apex.
ptbxl-7204.malfunction_evidence: Every spike captures; the intervals are constant.
teaching_points: 100% ventricular pacing with an LBBB-like V1 and superior axis = RV apical lead.
When the rhythm is fully paced, look between complexes for P waves to judge the underlying rhythm.
ptbxl-7204.notes: Machine read 'SRTH CHB VPR'. If dissociated P waves were confirmed, the answer would be VVI_CHB. Fine EMG noise in the baseline prevents a confident P-wave call.

ptbxl-13764.av_relationship: 1:1 conduction (PR ~200 ms, RBBB) for the first 7 beats; after the PVC the sinus P waves continue but the ventricle is paced, dissociated (P precedes the spikes by ~0.16 s and then ~0.05 s)
ptbxl-13764.beats: Sinus-conducted RBBB beats at ~0.35, 1.40, 2.43, 3.38, 4.53, 5.60, 6.68 s. PVC at ~7.43 s (tall in II, deep QS in V1). Ventricular paced at 8.73 s (possibly slight fusion) and 9.68 s.
ptbxl-13764.mode: VVI demand with rate hysteresis: escape after sensed beats >=1.15-1.3 s (a sinus RR of 1.15 s at 3.38-4.53 s was not paced; post-PVC escape ~1.3 s), then pacing at 0.94 s (~64 bpm)
ptbxl-13764.site_evidence: Paced beats appear only at 8.7-9.7 s (II, V4-V6, V1 strips). They are deeply negative in II, QS in V4-V5, negative in V6 and low-amplitude in V1. Probable RV apex; leads I/aVF not recorded for the paced beats.
ptbxl-13764.malfunction_evidence: The 1.3 s post-PVC pause is longer than the 0.94 s paced cycle, which fits programmed hysteresis rather than oversensing (no T-wave timing match).
ptbxl-13764.rates: sinus ~57 bpm; hysteresis escape ~1.3 s (~46 bpm); paced rate ~64 bpm (0.94 s)
teaching_points: Demand pacing: native sinus beats inhibit the device, and pacing appears only after the post-PVC pause.
Hysteresis: the escape interval after a sensed beat (~1.3 s) is longer than the paced interval (0.94 s), so do not call the pause oversensing.
Once pacing starts, the sinus P waves march through on their own (dissociation).
ptbxl-13764.notes: Machine read 'SBRAD OCC VPCX OCC PVC RBBB' fits. Hysteresis is inferred from timing only; the device settings are unknown.

ptbxl-20505.av_relationship: isorhythmic competition: during the paced run sinus P waves fall just (~30-40 ms) before each spike, too late to conduct; when the sinus rate edges above 60 the P waves conduct and take over
ptbxl-20505.beats: Fully paced: 0.37, 1.37, 2.37, 3.38, 4.38 s. Fusion: 5.37 s (spike, intermediate, smaller QRS). Pseudofusion: 6.38 s (spike on a native QRS). Intrinsic, inhibited: 7.30, 8.25 s. Pseudofusion: 9.25 s (small spike at QRS onset in V4-V6).
ptbxl-20505.mode: VVI at 60 bpm (1.0 s) with normal inhibition
ptbxl-20505.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~170 ms. II/III/aVF deep QS (superior axis); lead I small positive; aVL positive. V1 deep QS (LBBB-like). The native QRS is narrower, with rS in V1 and tall R in V4-V5.
ptbxl-20505.malfunction_evidence: The intrinsic beats at 7.30 and 8.25 s (RR 0.93-0.95 s) inhibit pacing; spikes appear only when an RR reaches 1.0 s.
ptbxl-20505.rates: lower rate 60 bpm (1.0 s); sinus ~60-65 bpm
teaching_points: One strip shows a full sequence: paced -> fusion (5.37 s) -> pseudofusion (6.38 s) -> intrinsic -> pseudofusion (9.25 s).
Fusion and pseudofusion happen when the native rate is close to the lower rate; they are normal.
The P waves just before the paced spikes are sinus P waves that are too late to conduct, not atrial tracking.
ptbxl-20505.notes: Machine read 'SRTH FREQ VPCX IVCB' fits. Excellent teaching strip for fusion and pseudofusion.

ptbxl-14956.atrial_rhythm: no P waves before the narrow beats; junctional escape rhythm ~60-65 bpm (sinus node dysfunction likely)
ptbxl-14956.av_relationship: no visible atrial activity; junctional beats compete with VVI pacing
ptbxl-14956.beats: Pseudofusion: 0.59 s (spike on a narrow QRS). Fully paced: 1.59, 2.59, 3.59, 4.59 s. Intrinsic narrow, inhibited: 5.53, 6.50 s. Pseudofusion: 7.53, 8.53 s (spike at the onset of an unchanged narrow QRS). Intrinsic: 9.39 s.
ptbxl-14956.mode: VVI at 60 bpm (1.0 s) with normal inhibition
ptbxl-14956.site_evidence: Paced QRS ~150 ms. II/III/aVF deep QS (superior axis); aVR and aVL positive; lead I small. V1 low-amplitude rs. The native QRS is narrow (~90 ms).
ptbxl-14956.malfunction_evidence: Intrinsic beats at RR 0.87-0.98 s inhibit pacing; spikes appear at ~1.0 s cycles, landing on the native QRS. A lone sharp transient in V4/V6 only at ~9.88 s is not in the II/V1 strips and is probably artifact.
ptbxl-14956.rates: lower rate 60 bpm (1.0 s); junctional rate ~60-68 bpm
teaching_points: VVI pacing at 60 bpm competes with a junctional rhythm at almost the same rate.
Spikes on narrow QRS complexes at 0.59, 7.53 and 8.53 s are pseudofusion, not loss of capture.
Beats arriving before 1.0 s are sensed and inhibit the pacemaker.
ptbxl-14956.notes: FUSION is an alternative answer. Machine read 'JUNCT-R FREQ VPCX' fits.

ptbxl-12000.atrial_rhythm: not assessable (precordial artifact); a possible P wave before the single intrinsic beat

A PVC just before the atrial spike is due inhibits the A output and resets timing
PVC coinciding with the A spike is followed by an early V spike (~100 ms) = ventricular safety pacing
